$comment:
The shared JSON-image case table. Executed byte-for-byte by
openbindings-go/formats/openapi, openapi-client/go, openapi-client/typescript
and openbindings-ts/packages/openapi (the last against that package's BUILT
dist, which is the shipped path it re-exports).

WHAT IT PINS. RFC 8259 Section 7 requires exactly three escapes inside a JSON
string -- quotation mark, reverse solidus, and U+0000 through U+001F -- and
then permits, without ever requiring, any other character to be escaped as a
six-character \uXXXX sequence. U+0026, U+003C and U+003E all fall inside its
`unescaped` production, so both spellings are conformant JSON.
openbindings.openapi@1 Section 9.2 preserves that permitted set and states no
preference inside it. Exactly one byte string still goes on the wire, so the
three engines make and document the same choice -- emit the literal
characters -- and this table is where that choice is held identical.

HOW THE EXPECTATIONS WERE AUTHORED. From three rules, never from an engine:
(1) RFC 8259 Section 7 plus the engines' literal-spelling convention for the
JSON image; (2) RFC 1866 Section 8.2.1 with RFC 1738 Section 2.2 for the
urlencoded CONTENT-path escaper, whose audit this table does not reopen; and
(3) RFC 6570 with allowReserved absent, i.e. RFC 3986's unreserved set, for
the STYLE path. The generator is
corpus-lab/scripts/build-json-image-table.mjs.

THE STYLE LANE IS THE CONTROL. The two urlencoded lanes are SUPPOSED to
spell a space differently, and the style lane expands an object's members as
separate name=value pairs without ever forming a JSON image. Not one of its
cells may move, and each engine asserts that separately from the cells.

EVERY CASE CARRIES ITS WHOLE OpenAPI DOCUMENT, and each engine loads that
document through its own shipped loader rather than building a typed model
directly. A harness that hands the engine a hand-built media object measures
an engine the project does not ship.

Every value is a SINGLE-KEY object so member ordering never enters the table:
Go sorts a map's keys and JavaScript preserves insertion order, and a twin
table must not pin a difference it is not about.

cases.name: 3.1.1|json-body|none
cases.basis: 3.1.1, the JSON request body. RFC 8259 §7 permits both the literal and the six-character spelling and requires neither (openbindings.openapi@1 §9.2, "The JSON image of an application value"); the engines' own documented convention is the literal one. the control: no character of the class appears, so no cell of any lane may move.

cases.name: 3.1.1|json-body|ampersand
cases.basis: 3.1.1, the JSON request body. RFC 8259 §7 permits both the literal and the six-character spelling and requires neither (openbindings.openapi@1 §9.2, "The JSON image of an application value"); the engines' own documented convention is the literal one. AMPERSAND U+0026, inside RFC 8259 §7's `unescaped = %x20-21 / %x23-5B / %x5D-10FFFF`.
